# 4.7 - Graphing Linear Inequalities {.unnumbered}

**Main Focus**

* Review inequality symbols and one-variable graphs.
* Graph two-variable inequalities ((y > mx + b), (y ≤ mx + b), etc.).
* Shade solution regions; test a point to verify.
* Interpret shaded regions in real-world terms.

> *Goal:* Extend linear models to represent ranges of possible solutions.

**Teacher Tips / Key Side Points**

* Link inequality symbols to boundary style: ≥ or ≤ → solid line; > or < → dashed line.
* Use color for shading; emphasize that shading = “all the answers.”
* Include one real-world tie-in (e.g., budgets, limits, maximum capacity).
* Quick check trick: (0,0) test point works most of the time.
* Reassure: “You’re not solving anything new—just graphing a rule with more answers.”
